test_title: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-I (Held On : 18 April 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He / can have been / more polite / to her.
solution:
The erroneous part is** "can have been"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the usage of **"can have been"** is incorrect instead of this we need to use** "can be"**
 
• The usage of "have been" after the modal verb is incorrect because we don't use passive voice structure in this way. The passive voice structure will be** "can + be + V₃". Though we don't have to use a passive voice in the given sentence.**
 
• "Can" means someone or something knows how to, is able to, is likely to, or has the right to do something.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• Can I be excused?
 
 

**Hence, the correct sentence is-** *He **can be** more polite to her.*
